summary: Palau's Division of Immigration says a tourist visa, valid for 30 days, may be issued on arrival to short-term travellers visiting for tourism, leisure or social visits; nationals of Bangladesh and Myanmar must apply before they reach Palau. It says FSM, Marshall Islands (RMI) and US citizens visiting Palau do not need a visa, citizens of Schengen states can stay without a visa for up to 90 days in any 180-day period, and citizens of Russia for 30 days. Every visitor is assessed a USD 100 environmental fee (PPEF), from which transit passengers and accredited diplomats are among those exempt, and all visitors must sign the Palau Pledge, stamped into their passports on arrival.

tips.text: The Division of Immigration says all visitors must sign the Palau Pledge on arrival, which is stamped into their passports, and that passengers must submit the Palau Entry Form at most 72 hours before departure; it generates a QR code to present on a mobile device or as a printed copy at check-in and on arrival.

The Division of Immigration says every international airline is required to include the USD 100 environmental fee (PPEF) in the price of the ticket into Palau. Exempt travellers, such as transit passengers and crew on official duty, can get a cash refund on arrival by presenting a travel itinerary showing the fee was paid and a passport.

The Koror State Government's fact sheet says visitors must have a valid Rock Island Use or Jellyfish Lake permit to use the Rock Islands Southern Lagoon area: the Rock Island Use permit costs $50.00 and the Jellyfish Lake permit $100.00 for all visitors aged 6 and above, and permits are valid for 10 days.

The UK government says it is illegal to bring reef-toxic sunscreen into Palau or to use it there, that customs officials will confiscate any found in your baggage, and that permitted sunscreens generally have an active ingredient of zinc oxide or titanium dioxide.

The UK government says Palau's only hyperbaric chamber is at the Belau National Hospital in Koror and that diving school standards are not always as high as in the UK. It advises making sure safety equipment, particularly oxygen, is available on the boat and asking about the ability to transfer divers to the hyperbaric chamber.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Palau?
faq.answer: For a holiday, Palau's Division of Immigration says a tourist visa, valid for 30 days, may be issued on arrival to short-term travellers visiting for tourism, leisure or social visits; your passport should be valid for at least six months at entry, you must possess a return ticket unless exempt, and you should have sufficient funds for your stay. It says FSM, Marshall Islands (RMI) and US citizens do not need a visa, citizens of Schengen states can stay without a visa for up to 90 days in any 180-day period, and nationals of Bangladesh and Myanmar must apply for the visa before they reach Palau.

faq.question: What is the Palau Pledge?
faq.answer: The Division of Immigration says all visitors must sign the Palau Pledge on arrival, which is stamped into their passports; it is a commitment to protect Palau's environment and culture for future generations. The UK government also says you must sign it.

faq.question: How much is Palau's environmental fee?
faq.answer: The Division of Immigration says every visitor coming to Palau is assessed a USD 100 environmental fee (PPEF), and every international airline is required to include it in the price of the ticket into Palau. Travellers with Palauan passports and their spouses, crew on official duty, accredited diplomats, transit passengers and others determined by the Minister of Finance are exempt and can get a cash refund on arrival by presenting a travel itinerary showing the fee was paid and a passport.

faq.question: Can I stay in Palau longer than 30 days?
faq.answer: Yes. The Division of Immigration says the tourist visa is valid for 30 days and may be extended for two additional 30-day periods; you must apply at least seven days before the expiration date of your current visa at the Division of Immigration, and the fee is USD 50 for renewal.

faq.question: Is sunscreen really banned in Palau?
faq.answer: Reef-toxic sunscreen is. The UK government says it is illegal to bring reef-toxic sunscreen into Palau or to use it there, that customs officials will confiscate any found in your baggage, and that there are penalties for selling it. It says permitted sunscreens generally have an active ingredient of zinc oxide or titanium dioxide.

You must apply at least seven days before the expiration date of your current visa at the Division of Immigration.
